extracted.intended_audience: press officers, communications/PR professionals, institutional media teams producing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for writing press releases that use inclusive, non-stigmatizing, and culturally aware language and imagery. Focuses on vocabulary, identity conventions (race, gender, disability, age, mental health, socioeconomic status), visual representation, and production practices that affect pickup and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Language is a powerful tool that can bring people together or drive them apart. Words create psychologically safe, inclusive, respectful, and welcoming environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language intentionally to foster psychological safety and inclusion; treat word choice as central to credibility and reception rather than optional 'political correctness.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive Language Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocabulary and descriptions that minimize bias, exhibit transparency, and show cultural awareness when referencing people, identities, and locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these characteristics across all text in a press release: be specific, avoid assumptions, and center accuracy and respect when naming identities and places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race and Ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific terms (e.g., 'Mexican American' rather than 'Hispanic/Latino' when accurate); capitalize Black, White, Indigenous, etc.; prefer 'people of color' over 'minorities'; note distinct ethnic identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise, self-identified labels; follow current capitalization conventions; avoid grouping diverse groups under imprecise or pejorative umbrella terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender and Sexual Orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use chosen names and pronouns; use 'LGBTQ+' or currently accepted acronyms; avoid gendered defaults (e.g., 'he/him'); use gender-neutral terms where appropriate; don't assume gender from name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask or confirm pronouns when possible, include pronouns for quoted individuals, and default to gender-neutral language when gender is unknown or irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use person-first language ('person with disability') OR identity-first ('disabled person') according to individual/community preference; avoid pity language ('suffers from'); avoid euphemisms ('differently abled').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the preference of the individual or community referenced; avoid language that conveys pity, diminishment, or euphemistic distancing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific age ranges; avoid 'elderly' (preferred: 'older adults'); avoid using 'youth' generically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about ages when relevant and avoid labels that are vague or potentially pejorative; consider context and agency of older or younger people in wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental Health and Substance Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use person-first terms ('person with substance use disorder'); avoid stigmatizing terms ('addict,' 'alcoholic'); use 'died by suicide' instead of 'committed suicide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize non-stigmatizing, clinical, and person-centered language; avoid criminalizing or moralizing phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Socioeconomic Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'poor' as an identity; use terms like 'low-income' or describe specific circumstances; avoid stereotypes and prefer describing specific situations rather than labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When socioeconomic status is relevant, describe conditions or metrics rather than assigning identity-defining labels; guard against implicit blame or stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image and Visual Inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use diverse representation in photos; avoid stereotypes in stock images; caption people specifically; show people in active roles; include visibility of people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select photos that reflect diversity in race, gender, age, ability, and socioeconomic context; write accurate captions and ensure visuals do not perpetuate stereotypes; include accessible image descriptions and representation of disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific identities used (not generic groupings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer naming specific identities rather than generic groupings in the press release text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace umbrella terms with precise identifiers when accuracy allows; be mindful of intra-group diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-identification respected
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect and use the self-identified terms of individuals and communities referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm preferred terms with sources where possible, and defer to community-specific nomenclature rather than external labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person-first or identity-first per community preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply person-first ('person with disability') or identity-first ('disabled person') constructions according to community or individual preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and follow the preference; when unsure, check guidance from relevant advocacy groups or the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization conventions current
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow current conventions for capitalizing identity labels (e.g., capitalize Black, White, Indigenous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep style updated with major style guide changes and community preferences; review capitalization policies periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-neutral where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use gender-neutral language when gender is not relevant or known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use singular 'they' or neutral terms (e.g., 'chair' instead of 'chairman') and avoid defaulting to masculine pronouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronouns specified per individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify and use individuals' chosen pronouns in text and captions where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pronouns in speaker identifications, bylines, or quoted attributions when relevant and with consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stigmatizing language (mental health, substance use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use stigmatizing, moralizing, or dehumanizing language for mental health or substance use issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose clinical, person-centered terminology and avoid labels that reduce people to a condition or behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific age ranges (not 'elderly')
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific ages or age ranges instead of generic terms like 'elderly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the exact age or age bracket when it matters; avoid ageist language and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'minorities' as default
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not default to the term 'minorities' to describe groups of non-dominant identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more precise descriptors (e.g., specific racial/ethnic groups, 'people of color' when appropriate) and avoid reductive grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple voices represented
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multiple voices or perspectives in the release where applicable, especially from the communities discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote diverse sources, include community spokespeople, and avoid single-source narratives about a community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use images that show a range of identities and avoid tokenism or stereotypical portrayals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images showing people in varied roles and contexts, reflecting genuine diversity rather than staged or stereotyped depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific, accurate captions for images and identify people appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions should name people, describe action/context, and avoid reductive or identity-first framing without consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include accessibility measures such as alt text, visible inclusion of people with disabilities, and other accessible formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure images have descriptive alt text, provide release content in accessible file formats, and represent accessibility in visuals and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid language and images that rely on or perpetuate stereotypes about groups of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review for implicit associations, clichéd roles, and framing that assigns traits to whole groups; consult sensitivity readers when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Have content reviewed for cultural sensitivity before distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensitivity readers, consult community members, or obtain native-speaker review for culturally specific content or translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Considerations: update and consult
rubrics_metrics.description: Update terminology as language evolves; consult community preferences; use native speaker review and sensitivity readers for sensitive topics; maintain style guide consistency; go beyond 'political correctness' to accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat terminology as dynamic—periodically review and update organizational guidance; incorporate external community input and specialist reviewers for high-sensitivity material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on pickup and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases violating inclusive language standards may be edited heavily or rejected by major news outlets; sources flagged for offensive language lose credibility; modern audiences expect inclusive framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to inclusive language increases the likelihood of pickup and preserves institutional credibility; consider editorial policies of target outlets when drafting releases.
